jobs.title: Senior Manager, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
At PDI Technologies, we empower some of the world's leading convenience retail and petroleum brands with cutting-edge technology solutions that drive growth and operational efficiency. By “Connecting Convenience” across the globe, we empower businesses to increase productivity, make more informed decisions, and engage faster with customers through loyalty programs, shopper insights, and unmatched real-time market intelligence via mobile applications, such as GasBuddy.  We’re a global team committed to excellence, collaboration, and driving real impact. Explore our opportunities and become part of a company that values diversity, integrity, and growth.

Role Overview

You will own how data gets into our platform and how it gets served back out — ingestion, the lakehouse, and the query layer underneath everything analytics and product depend on. 

The problem is specific. Data arrives from CDC streams, transactional databases, event topics, partner APIs, and files, and today each source carries its own pipeline, its own failure modes, and its own on-call story. Your mandate is to collapse that into one ingestion framework and one open lakehouse — reliable enough to publish SLOs against, fast enough to serve interactive query, and cheap enough to defend line by line. 

This is a hands-on role. You will set technical direction, hire, and grow the team — and you will also be in design reviews, in code review, and in the pipeline when a stateful stream will not recover from its checkpoint. Expect roughly half your time in technical work. 

You own the full path: how data lands, the table format and its lifecycle, the transformation layer, the engines that serve it, and the SLOs on top of all of it. When a dataset is late or wrong, it is your team's phone that rings — and you are expected to have already built the thing that catches it first.

What you will do:

Lead, hire, and grow a team of 10+ data engineers — set the technical bar through design and code review, not through status meetings. 

Own the architecture and delivery of a unified ingestion framework: one configuration-driven path for batch, CDC, and streaming sources, with schema evolution, replay and backfill, idempotency, dead-letter handling, and data contracts built into the framework rather than reimplemented per pipeline. 

Own production Spark Structured Streaming pipelines — watermarking, stateful joins and aggregations, checkpoint and restart discipline, exactly-once sinks, lag and backpressure management. 

Own the Apache Iceberg lakehouse: partition and sort strategy, file sizing and compaction, snapshot and orphan-file lifecycle, schema and partition evolution, and multi-engine interoperability. 

Set the dbt modeling standard — layering conventions, tests, contracts, CI enforcement, and lineage that stakeholders trust. 

Own Trino catalog design, workload isolation, and query performance for interactive and federated access. 

Define and meet freshness, completeness, and latency SLOs. Run a 24x7 on-call rotation with a short mean time to restore. 

Own cost: a defensible cost-per-pipeline and cost-per-dataset number, and the levers to move it. 

Partner with product, analytics, and architecture to sequence the roadmap, and bring rigor to decisions — collect the data, seek dissent, and run pilots rather than arguing from opinion

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience directly managing data engineers and/or analytics engineers, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.

Experience managing both a data engineering and an analytics engineering function specifically, rather than one or the other.

Ventiva is a leader in active cooling solutions for electronic devices, delivering thinner, faster, and cooler high-performance products that remain lightweight, silent, and vibration-free. We are seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Infrastructure Maturity & Assessment to lead rigorous baseline assessments and maturity evaluations of enterprise infrastructure estates, translating findings into financially grounded future-state roadmaps that clients can fund and execute. This role is built for advisors who bring genuine depth across infrastructure domains — people who know what good looks like across modern practice, can measure the gap with precision, and can build the TCO and investment cases that turn an assessment into a board-level decision. Run infrastructure maturity assessments — applying structured maturity models across compute, network, storage, cloud, operations, and tooling to establish a credible, evidence-based baseline of where a client currently sits against modern practice

Define the future state — translating assessment findings into a well-reasoned target architecture and operating model that reflects both best-practice ambition and the commercial and organizational constraints of the client

Build the financial case — developing TCO models, infrastructure rationalization business cases, and investment scenarios that quantify the cost of current-state technical debt alongside the financial return of modernization

Construct the roadmap — producing phased, prioritized transformation roadmaps that sequence initiatives by value, risk, and dependency, with clear investment requirements and measurable outcomes at each stage

Present findings to CIO and senior technology audiences — communicating assessment outcomes, maturity gaps, and investment recommendations with the clarity and credibility needed to drive executive sponsorship and funding approval

Develop and maintain Accenture's assessment methodology and maturity frameworks — keeping benchmarks current against evolving cloud, automation, and operational practice, and codifying findings into reusable intellectual property

Support business development — using assessment engagements as the entry point for longer transformation programs, shaping downstream delivery proposals and maintaining client relationships through the advisory-to-execution handoff

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 25% to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Minimum 8+ years of progressive experience in IT infrastructure, infrastructure architecture, or technology consulting — with sufficient depth across domains to assess maturity credibly and benchmark against modern practice

Experience developing or stewarding a proprietary infrastructure maturity framework — including ongoing calibration of benchmarks as cloud, automation, and operational best practice evolves

Deep sector experience in financial services, manufacturing, energy, or public sector, where infrastructure assessments intersect with regulatory obligation, operational risk, and multi-year capital planning cycles

Industry certifications across cloud architecture, infrastructure, or enterprise architecture (AWS, Azure, GCP, TOGAF, or equivalent); familiarity with frameworks such as CMMI, ISO/IEC 38500, or cloud adoption maturity models

Maturity Modelling & Baseline Assessment: Structured infrastructure domain maturity frameworks, evidence-based current-state gap analysis, and competitive/regulatory peer benchmarking.

At PDI Technologies, we empower some of the world's leading convenience retail and petroleum brands with cutting-edge technology solutions that drive growth and operational efficiency. By “Connecting Convenience” across the globe, we empower businesses to increase productivity, make more informed decisions, and engage faster with customers through loyalty programs, shopper insights, and unmatched real-time market intelligence via mobile applications, such as GasBuddy.  We’re a global team committed to excellence, collaboration, and driving real impact. Explore our opportunities and become part of a company that values diversity, integrity, and growth.

Role Overview

You will own how data gets into our platform and how it gets served back out — ingestion, the lakehouse, and the query layer underneath everything analytics and product depend on. 

The problem is specific. Data arrives from CDC streams, transactional databases, event topics, partner APIs, and files, and today each source carries its own pipeline, its own failure modes, and its own on-call story. Your mandate is to collapse that into one ingestion framework and one open lakehouse — reliable enough to publish SLOs against, fast enough to serve interactive query, and cheap enough to defend line by line. 

This is a hands-on role. You will set technical direction, hire, and grow the team — and you will also be in design reviews, in code review, and in the pipeline when a stateful stream will not recover from its checkpoint. Expect roughly half your time in technical work. 

You own the full path: how data lands, the table format and its lifecycle, the transformation layer, the engines that serve it, and the SLOs on top of all of it. When a dataset is late or wrong, it is your team's phone that rings — and you are expected to have already built the thing that catches it first.

What you will do:

Lead, hire, and grow a team of 10+ data engineers — set the technical bar through design and code review, not through status meetings. 

Own the architecture and delivery of a unified ingestion framework: one configuration-driven path for batch, CDC, and streaming sources, with schema evolution, replay and backfill, idempotency, dead-letter handling, and data contracts built into the framework rather than reimplemented per pipeline. 

Own production Spark Structured Streaming pipelines — watermarking, stateful joins and aggregations, checkpoint and restart discipline, exactly-once sinks, lag and backpressure management. 

Own the Apache Iceberg lakehouse: partition and sort strategy, file sizing and compaction, snapshot and orphan-file lifecycle, schema and partition evolution, and multi-engine interoperability. 

Set the dbt modeling standard — layering conventions, tests, contracts, CI enforcement, and lineage that stakeholders trust. 

Own Trino catalog design, workload isolation, and query performance for interactive and federated access. 

Define and meet freshness, completeness, and latency SLOs. Run a 24x7 on-call rotation with a short mean time to restore. 

Own cost: a defensible cost-per-pipeline and cost-per-dataset number, and the levers to move it. 

Partner with product, analytics, and architecture to sequence the roadmap, and bring rigor to decisions — collect the data, seek dissent, and run pilots rather than arguing from opinion

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. 

8+ years in data engineering, including 3+ years leading engineers as a manager or tech lead — and you are still hands-on in code and design. 

Production experience with Spark Structured Streaming at scale: state store growth, checkpoint recovery, watermark tuning, and late or out-of-order data. 

Deep Apache Spark and PySpark performance work — diagnosing and fixing skew, shuffle pressure, small-file problems, and executor memory failures on real workloads. 

Experience building or substantially owning a reusable ingestion framework serving multiple source types — not a collection of individual pipelines. 

Production experience with an open table format (Apache Iceberg preferred) including schema and partition evolution, compaction strategy, and migration from an existing format. 

Experience with dbt as a team-wide modeling standard, including testing and CI. 

Experience with Trino or Presto operations and query optimization. 

Experience running reliable, high-scale platform systems — 24x7 on-call, availability targets, and fast restoration of service

Preferred Qualifications

Apache Flink, Kafka or MSK internals, or high-throughput stream-join design. 

CDC tooling in production (Debezium, DMS, GoldenGate, Qlik) and integrating legacy or mainframe sources into modern pipelines. 

Data contracts, catalog, and lineage tooling (DataHub, OpenMetadata, Glue, Unity). 

Iceberg REST catalog implementations and multi-engine interoperability. 

AWS, Kubernetes, and Terraform fluency — you can debug below the framework layer. 

Multi-tenant B2B data platforms with per-tenant cost attribution and isolation. 

Open-source contribution to the projects in this stack.

About Ventiva

Ventiva is a leader in active cooling solutions for electronic devices, delivering thinner, faster, and cooler high-performance products that remain lightweight, silent, and vibration-free. Its patented Ionic Cooling Engine (ICE) technology provides an all-electronic heat transfer solution that addresses thermal challenges in modern high-performance semiconductor design. ICE technology generates airflow without moving parts by using electrohydrodynamic (EHD) principles to move ionized air molecules within an electric field. Ventiva’s ICE9 thermal management suite offers smart, adaptive cooling that continuously monitors system needs and adjusts airflow accordingly. By combining advanced monitoring, algorithms, and real-time software, ICE9 supports robust, device-wide thermal management integrated with overall system performance.

About the Role

The Director, Applications Engineering is a full-time, on-site role based in Fremont, CA. This role leads the applications engineering function, guiding the integration of Ventiva’s ICE and ICE9 technologies into customer systems and reference designs. The director collaborates closely with product, software, and hardware teams to define requirements, validate performance, and resolve complex thermal and system-level challenges. Day-to-day responsibilities include managing engineering projects, overseeing customer evaluations and proof-of-concept builds, providing technical leadership to the applications engineering team, and ensuring timely, high-quality delivery of solutions. The role also involves engaging with key customers and partners, supporting pre- and post-sales technical activities, and contributing to product roadmaps and application guidelines based on real-world use cases.

Demonstrated Team Leadership skills, including mentoring, performance management, and building high-performing, cross-functional engineering teams.

Track record hiring and running a distributed applications team, including Taiwan/Greater China.

At Hopscotch Primary Care, we believe great healthcare should be accessible to all people across all communities. Our patients and the care teams who serve them sit at the center of everything we do at Hopscotch. Hopscotch Primary Care takes a team approach to serve patient needs and provide the best care possible. Our goal is to provide the care each of us would want for ourselves or for our family members, in the right setting, and at the right time.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Infrastructure Maturity & Assessment to lead rigorous baseline assessments and maturity evaluations of enterprise infrastructure estates, translating findings into financially grounded future-state roadmaps that clients can fund and execute. This role is built for advisors who bring genuine depth across infrastructure domains — people who know what good looks like across modern practice, can measure the gap with precision, and can build the TCO and investment cases that turn an assessment into a board-level decision. The output of this work is not a report: it is a prioritized, costed roadmap that a client organization can commit to and a delivery team can run.

Run infrastructure maturity assessments — applying structured maturity models across compute, network, storage, cloud, operations, and tooling to establish a credible, evidence-based baseline of where a client currently sits against modern practice

Define the future state — translating assessment findings into a well-reasoned target architecture and operating model that reflects both best-practice ambition and the commercial and organizational constraints of the client

Build the financial case — developing TCO models, infrastructure rationalization business cases, and investment scenarios that quantify the cost of current-state technical debt alongside the financial return of modernization

Construct the roadmap — producing phased, prioritized transformation roadmaps that sequence initiatives by value, risk, and dependency, with clear investment requirements and measurable outcomes at each stage

Present findings to CIO and senior technology audiences — communicating assessment outcomes, maturity gaps, and investment recommendations with the clarity and credibility needed to drive executive sponsorship and funding approval

Develop and maintain Accenture's assessment methodology and maturity frameworks — keeping benchmarks current against evolving cloud, automation, and operational practice, and codifying findings into reusable intellectual property

Support business development — using assessment engagements as the entry point for longer transformation programs, shaping downstream delivery proposals and maintaining client relationships through the advisory-to-execution handoff

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 25% to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Required Qualificiations:

Minimum 8+ years of progressive experience in IT infrastructure, infrastructure architecture, or technology consulting — with sufficient depth across domains to assess maturity credibly and benchmark against modern practice

Minimum 8+ years in advisory or architecture leadership roles, with a track record of delivering infrastructure assessments, target state designs, and transformation roadmaps for large, complex enterprise clients

Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience)

Experience developing or stewarding a proprietary infrastructure maturity framework — including ongoing calibration of benchmarks as cloud, automation, and operational best practice evolves

Deep sector experience in financial services, manufacturing, energy, or public sector, where infrastructure assessments intersect with regulatory obligation, operational risk, and multi-year capital planning cycles

Industry certifications across cloud architecture, infrastructure, or enterprise architecture (AWS, Azure, GCP, TOGAF, or equivalent); familiarity with frameworks such as CMMI, ISO/IEC 38500, or cloud adoption maturity models
